titleEn: The Glory of Kings — Solomon’s Weeping and the Angel’s Prophecy (ch. 67)
part: ch. 67 — Solomon’s Weeping and the Angel’s Prophecy
about: Solomon, sick at sixty and struck by the angel of death, prays for mercy, and an angel of the Lord answers with a rebuke for his many wives and a prophecy of three sons. The Saviour will come from his line and, as Joseph, Moses and Joshua did for Israel, bring his kin out of Sheol.

sentences.t: ፷ወ፯ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ብካየ ፡ ሰሎሞን ።
sentences.l: 60-and-7. Concerning weeping-of Solomon
sentences.i: Chapter 67: Concerning the weeping of Solomon
sentences.n: Chapter heading. ፷ወ፯ is 60 + ወ- ‘and’ + 7 (Ethiopic numerals: tens, then ones). በእንተ ‘concerning’ governs a construct chain: ብካየ is ብካይ ‘weeping’ in the construct/accusative form in -ä, so ‘weeping-of Solomon’.

sentences.t: ወዘከመሂ ፡ አዕረፈ ፡ እነግረክሙ ፤
sentences.l: And-how-indeed he-rested I-will-tell-you
sentences.i: And I will tell you how he died;
sentences.n: ወዘከመሂ = ወ- ‘and’ + ዘከመ ‘how, in the way that’ + the enclitic -ሂ (a light emphasis, ‘also, indeed’; the house gloss reads ‘however, in whatever way’, and a plain ‘how’ suits this clause). አዕረፈ ‘he rested’ is the usual euphemism for ‘died’ (3ms perfect, causative stem). እነግረክሙ = እ- (1cs imperfect/subjunctive) of ነገረ ‘tell’ + -ክሙ ‘you (pl.)’. The ‘how’-clause comes first, the main verb last.

sentences.t: ኮነ ፡ መዋዕሊሁ ፡ ፷ ፡ ወአኀዞ ፡ ሕማም ፡ ወበከመ ፡ መዋዕለ ፡ አቡሁሰ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ኢኮነ ፡ አላ ፡ ፳ ፡ ሐጸ ፡ እምኔሁ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ዘተአዘዘ ፡ ለአንስት ፡ ወሰገደ ፡ ለጣዖታት ።
sentences.l: Were his-days 60, and-seized-him sickness, and-as days-of his-father-indeed David not-was but 20: he-fell-short from-him on-account-of that-he-obeyed to-women and-bowed to-idols.
sentences.i: His days numbered sixty, and sickness took hold of him. He did not match the days of his father David but fell short of him by twenty (?), because he submitted to women and bowed down to idols.
sentences.n: ኮነ is 3ms (‘it was’) with a plural subject መዋዕሊሁ ‘his days’ (መዋዕል + -ሁ); the numeral ፷ is ‘sixty’ (years understood). ወአኀዞ = ወ- + አኀዘ ‘seized’ + -ኦ ‘him’. በከመ … -ሰ ‘as for the days of his father David’ (-ሰ marks the contrast). ኢኮነ አላ ፳ … ሐጸ እምኔሁ is compressed: ‘it was not (so), but twenty: he fell short of him (ሐጸ, 3ms perfect; the sense ‘fall short, lack’ is taken from context (?)) by comparison’; my reading of ፳ as ‘twenty short’ is a judgment (?). ዘተአዘዘ ለአንስት: በእንተ ዘ- ‘because of the fact that’ + ተአዘዘ, the T-stem of አዘዘ ‘command’, whose usual sense is ‘obey, submit to’ (rather than the passive ‘was commanded’), with ለ- ‘to’ marking the one obeyed, ‘women’. Compare 1 Kings 11:1–8 (Solomon’s foreign wives and their gods).

sentences.t: ወመጽአ ፡ መልአከ ፡ ሞት ፡ ወዘበጦ ፡ እግሮ ፡ ወበከየ ፡ ወይቤ ፡ እግዚኦ ፡ አምላከ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ እስመ ፡ ሕገ ፡ መሬታዊ ፡ ተመዋእኩ ፡ እስመ ፡ አልቦ ፡ ንጹሐ ፡ እምርስሐት ፡ በቅድሜከ ፡ እግዚኦ ፡ ወአልቦ ፡ ዘይጸድቅ ፡ ወይጠብብ ፡ በቅድሜከ ፡ እግዚኦ ፡ እስመ ፡ አንተ ፡ ትሬኢ ፡ ወትፈትን ፡ ልበ ፡ ወአልቦ ፡ ዘይሴወር ፡ እምኔከ ፡ ኅቡኣተ ፡ ትሬኢ ፡ በክሡታት ፡ ወልበ ፡ ተሐትት ፡ መሐረኒ ፡ እግዚኦ ፤
sentences.l: And-came angel-of death and-struck-him his-foot, and-wept and-said: O-Lord, God-of Israel, for law-of earthly I-have-been-overcome; for not-is [one] clean from-filth before-you, O-Lord, and-not-is [one] who-is-righteous and-is-wise before-you, O-Lord; for you see and-test heart, and-not-is [one] who-is-hidden from-you; hidden-things you-see among-open-things, and-heart you-examine; have-mercy-on-me, O-Lord;
sentences.i: The angel of death came and struck his foot, and he wept and said: “Lord, God of Israel, for I have been overcome by the law of earthly beings; for no one is clean of filth before you, Lord; and no one is righteous and wise before you, Lord. You see and test the heart, and no one is hidden from you; you see hidden things among the things laid open (?), and you examine the heart. Have mercy on me, Lord;
sentences.n: Narrative verbs are 3ms perfects with ወ-: ወመጽአ ‘and came’, ወዘበጦ ‘and struck him’ (ዘበጠ + -ኦ; the foot, እግሮ, is a second accusative), ወበከየ ‘and wept’, ወይቤ ‘and said’; the prayer starts after ወይቤ. መልአከ ሞት is construct, ‘angel-of death’. እግዚኦ is the vocative ‘O Lord’; እስራኤል depends on the construct አምላከ. ተመዋእኩ is the T-stem passive of መወአ ‘conquer’, 1cs perfect (-ኩ), ‘I have been conquered’ (the stem is my reading) (?); ሕገ መሬታዊ ‘law of the earthly’ I take as ‘the law of mortal creatures’ (?). አልቦ ‘there is not’ takes the accusative: ንጹሐ ‘a clean one’. ዘይጸድቅ ወይጠብብ = ዘ- ‘one who’ + 3ms imperfects ‘is righteous, is wise’. ትሬኢ ‘you see’, ትፈትን ‘you test’, ተሐትት ‘you examine’ are 2ms imperfects. ዘይሴወር ‘who is hidden’ is a passive-sense imperfect of ሰወረ ‘hide’; the exact stem is uncertain (?). ኅቡኣተ ትሬኢ በክሡታት is terse: ‘hidden things you see among/in open ones’ (?). The refrain መሐረኒ እግዚኦ = መሐረ (imperative 2ms) + -ኒ ‘me’, repeated through the prayer. The thought, that no one is blameless before God, echoes Psalm 143:2 and Job 4:17.

sentences.t: ልበ ፡ ሰብእ ፡ ተኀሥሥ ፡ ወኵልያተ ፡ ትፈትን ፡ መሐረኒ ፡ እግዚኦ ፤
sentences.l: Heart-of man you-search and-kidneys you-test; have-mercy-on-me, O-Lord;
sentences.i: You search the heart of man and test the inner parts; have mercy on me, Lord;
sentences.n: ልበ ሰብእ is a construct chain (‘heart-of man’) as the object of ተኀሥሥ (2ms imperfect of ኀሠሠ ‘search’). ኵልያተ is the accusative plural of ኵልያት ‘kidneys’, the seat of feeling and conscience; ትፈትን ‘you test’. This is the biblical formula of God as examiner of hearts and kidneys (Psalm 7:9; Jeremiah 17:10).

sentences.t: ዘልሑሳስ ፡ ወዘረዓም ፡ ትሰምዕ ፡ መሐረኒ ፡ እግዚኦ ፤
sentences.l: That-of-soft-speech(?) and-that-of-thunder you-hear; have-mercy-on-me, O-Lord;
sentences.i: You hear the faint (?) and the thunderous; have mercy on me, Lord;
sentences.n: ዘ- ‘that which’ heads two objects: ዘልሑሳስ ‘that of whisper(ing)’ and ዘረዓም ‘that of thunder (loud noise)’; ትሰምዕ is the 2ms imperfect ‘you hear’. The meaning of ልሑሳስ is uncertain to me, and I take it as ‘whispered, faint’ from context, perhaps related to ልሑስ ‘soft, tender’ (?). The point is a merism: God hears the quietest and the loudest speech.

sentences.t: ወእመሰ ፡ መሐርኮሙ ፡ ለጻድቃን ፡ እለ ፡ ኢተዐደዉ ፡ እምትእዛዝከ ፡ ምንት ፡ መንክር ፡ ምሕረትከ ፡ መሐረኒ ፡ እግዚኦ ፤
sentences.l: And-if-indeed you-had-mercy-on-them to-the-righteous who not-they-transgressed from-your-commandment, what wonderful your-mercy? Have-mercy-on-me, O-Lord;
sentences.i: If you have shown mercy to the righteous, who have not transgressed your commandment, what is wonderful about your mercy? Have mercy on me, Lord;
sentences.n: ወእመሰ = ወ- + እመ ‘if’ + -ሰ (contrast). መሐርኮሙ = መሐረ ‘have mercy’, 2ms perfect (-ከ), + -ሙ ‘them’; ለጻድቃን restates the object with ለ-. እለ ‘who (pl.)’ + ኢተዐደዉ, 3mp perfect of ተዐደወ ‘pass beyond, transgress’, with እም- ‘from’ (‘overstepped’, ‘gone beyond’); ትእዛዝከ ‘your commandment’ (ትእዛዝ + -ከ). ምንት መንክር is a verbless question: ‘what (is) wonderful?’; ምሕረትከ ‘your mercy’.

sentences.t: አላ ፡ ሶበ ፡ ትምሕር ፡ ኪያየ ፡ ኃጥአ ፡ ውእቱኬ ፡ መንክር ፡ ወአዳም ፡ ምሕረትከ ፡ መሐረኒ ፡ እግዚኦ ፤
sentences.l: But when you-have-mercy me, sinner, that-indeed wonderful and-pleasing(?) your-mercy; have-mercy-on-me, O-Lord;
sentences.i: But when you have mercy on me, a sinner, that is wonderful and pleasing (?), your mercy; have mercy on me, Lord;
sentences.n: ሶበ ‘when’ + ትምሕር, 2ms imperfect of መሐረ. ኪያየ is the independent accusative pronoun ‘me’ (ኪያ- + -የ), with ኃጥአ ‘sinner’ (accusative) in apposition. ውእቱኬ = ውእቱ ‘that’ + the emphatic enclitic -ኬ (‘that indeed’). መንክር ‘wonderful’ stands without a copula. The meaning of አዳም here is uncertain (?): I read it as an adjective ‘pleasing’ (?) matching መንክር, not the name Adam. The sentence is the answer to the previous one: mercy to the righteous is nothing remarkable, mercy to a sinner is.

sentences.t: ሶበ ፡ አነ ፡ አበስኩ ፡ ተዘከር ፡ አብርሃም ፡ ወይስሐቅ ፡ ወያዕቆብ ፡ አበዊየ ፡ እለ ፡ ኢተዐደዉ ፡ እምትእዛዝከ ፡ መሐረኒ ፡ እግዚኦ ፤
sentences.l: When I I-sinned, remember Abraham and-Isaac and-Jacob, my-fathers, who not-they-transgressed from-your-commandment; have-mercy-on-me, O-Lord;
sentences.i: Since I have sinned, remember Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, my fathers, who did not transgress your commandment; have mercy on me, Lord;
sentences.n: ሶበ is ‘when’ but here ‘since, seeing that’. አነ አበስኩ = ‘I’ (independent pronoun) + 1cs perfect of አበሰ ‘sin’. ተዘከር is the imperative 2ms of ተዘከረ ‘remember’; the three patriarchs are its objects, ወ- joining them. አበዊየ ‘my fathers’ = አበው (plural of አብ) + -የ ‘my’. The plea, to be forgiven for the sake of the sinless patriarchs, echoes the Prayer of Manasseh, verse 8.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ መሓሪ ፡ ወሰራዪ ፡ አንተ ፡ እግዚኦ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ዳዊት ፡ ገብርከ ፡ መሐረኒ ፡ እግዚኦ ፤
sentences.l: For merciful and-forgiver you, O-Lord; for-the-sake-of David your-servant, have-mercy-on-me, O-Lord;
sentences.i: For you are merciful and forgiving, Lord; for the sake of David your servant, have mercy on me, Lord;
sentences.n: A verbless sentence: እስመ ‘for’ + two agent nouns, መሓሪ ‘one who shows mercy’ and ሰራዪ ‘one who forgives’ (from the root s-r-y ‘forgive’), + አንተ ‘you’. በእንተ ‘for the sake of’ takes ዳዊት, and ገብርከ = ገብር ‘servant’ + -ከ ‘your’ is in apposition. ‘For David’s sake’ is the language of Psalm 132:10 and 1 Kings 11:12–13.

sentences.t: አኃዜ ፡ ዓለም ፡ ወነገሥት ፡ ወመኳንንት ፡ መሐረኒ ፡ እግዚኦ ፤
sentences.l: Holder-of world and-kings and-rulers, have-mercy-on-me, O-Lord;
sentences.i: You who hold the world, kings and rulers: have mercy on me, Lord;
sentences.n: From here to the end of the prayer, each line opens with a vocative epithet. አኃዜ is the construct of አኃዚ ‘one who seizes, holds’ (agent noun); its dependents are ዓለም ‘world’ and the plural nouns ነገሥት ‘kings’ and መኳንንት ‘rulers, nobles’, joined by ወ-. Whether ‘holder of’ means ‘ruler over’ or ‘seizer of’ is not settled by the grammar; the context favours ‘ruler of’.

sentences.t: መጥበቤ ፡ አብዳን ፡ ወማእበዴ ፡ ጠቢባን ፡ መሐረኒ ፡ እግዚኦ ፤
sentences.l: Wise-making-of fools and-fool-making-of wise-men, have-mercy-on-me, O-Lord;
sentences.i: You who make fools wise and the wise foolish: have mercy on me, Lord;
sentences.n: A matched pair of agent nouns in the construct: መጥበቤ ‘one who makes wise’ (causative of ጠበበ ‘be wise’) governing አብዳን ‘fools’, and ማእበዴ ‘one who makes foolish’ (causative of አበደ ‘be foolish’) governing ጠቢባን ‘wise ones’. Both forms are unusual and I read them from the parallelism (?). Compare 1 Corinthians 1:20–27, where God makes the world’s wisdom foolish and chooses the foolish to shame the wise.

sentences.t: መያጤ ፡ ኃጥኣን ፡ ወዐሳዬ ፡ ጻድቃን ፡ መሐረኒ ፡ እግዚኦ ።
sentences.l: Repayer-of sinners and-rewarder-of righteous, have-mercy-on-me, O-Lord.
sentences.i: You who repay sinners and reward the righteous: have mercy on me, Lord.
sentences.n: Another pair of agent nouns in the construct: መያጤ ‘one who requites’ (from መየጠ ‘repay, requite’) + ኃጥኣን ‘sinners’, and ዐሳዬ ‘one who rewards’ (from ዐሰየ, the root of ዕሴት ‘reward’) + ጻድቃን ‘righteous ones’. Both meanings are inferred, not checked (?). The sentence ends with ። and so closes the prayer.

sentences.t: ወዘንተ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብል ፡ ይውሕዝ ፡ አንብዑ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ገጹ ፡ ወየኀሥሥ ፡ በሰበኑ ፨
sentences.l: And-this while he-says, flows his-tears onto his-face, and-he-seeks with-his-cloth.
sentences.i: While he was saying this, his tears ran down his face, and he wiped them (?) with his cloth.
sentences.n: ወዘንተ = ወ- + ዘንተ, the accusative of ዝ ‘this’, object of the circumstantial clause እንዘ ይብል ‘while he says’ (እንዘ + imperfect). ይውሕዝ ‘flows’ (3ms imperfect), subject አንብዑ ‘his tears’ (አንብዕ + -ሁ); ውስተ ገጹ ‘onto his face’. የኀሥሥ is 3ms imperfect of ኀሠሠ, normally ‘search, seek’; ‘wipe’ is a guess from the context with በሰበኑ ‘with his cloth’ (ሰበን ‘linen cloth’) (?). The sign ፨ closes the unit and shifts to the angel’s speech.

sentences.t: ወወረደ ፡ ኀቤሁ ፡ መልአከ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወይቤሎ ፡ ስማዕ ፡ ዘእነግረከ ፡ ዘለአከኒ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፤
sentences.l: And-descended to-him angel-of Lord and-said-to-him: Listen that-which I-tell-you, that-which-sent-me Lord;
sentences.i: The angel of the Lord came down to him and said to him: “Listen to what I tell you, that with which the Lord has sent me (?);
sentences.n: Verbs: ወወረደ ‘and descended’ (3ms perfect), ወይቤሎ = ይቤ ‘said’ + -ሎ ‘to him’. ኀቤሁ = ኀበ ‘to’ + -ሁ ‘him’. መልአከ እግዚኣብሔር is a construct chain, presumably a different angel from the angel of death. ስማዕ is the imperative 2ms ‘listen’. ዘእነግረከ = ዘ- ‘that which’ + እነግረከ, 1cs imperfect of ነገረ + -ከ ‘you’; ዘለአከኒ = ዘ- ‘who’ + ለአከ ‘sent’ (3ms perfect) + -ኒ ‘me’. I take ዘለአከኒ እግዚኣብሔር as a second relative clause on the message, ‘that which the Lord sent me (with)’, since ዘ- ordinarily points to a thing; the alternative, ‘the Lord who sent me’, would need ዘ- to stand for a person (?).

sentences.t: እንዘ ፡ ጠቢብአ ፡ አብደ ፡ ረሰይከ ፡ ርእስከ ፡ ወእንዘ ፡ ባዕል ፡ አንደይከ ፡ ርእስከ ፡ ወእንዘ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ አኅሰርከ ፡ ርእስከ ፡ በተዐድዎ ፡ ትእዛዘ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፤
sentences.l: While wise foolish you-made your-head, and-while rich you-made-poor your-head, and-while king you-ruined your-head by-transgressing commandment-of Lord;
sentences.i: Though wise, you made yourself a fool; though rich, you made yourself poor; though a king, you brought yourself to ruin, by transgressing the commandment of the Lord;
sentences.n: Three parallel clauses, each of the form እንዘ ‘while (being)’ + a noun (ጠቢብ, ባዕል, ንጉሥ) — a verbless circumstantial clause. ርእስ ‘head’ + -ከ is the reflexive ‘yourself’. Verbs are 2ms perfects: ረሰይከ (ረሰየ ‘make’), አንደይከ (causative of ነደየ ‘be poor’), አኅሰርከ (causative of ኀሰረ ‘suffer loss’). ጠቢብአ is written with a final አ; read as ጠቢብ (the final አ is unexplained; it may be a slip for the accusative ጠቢበ) (?). አብደ is the accusative ‘a fool’ (predicate of ረሰይከ). በተዐድዎ = በ- ‘by’ + ተዐድዎ, the verbal noun ‘transgressing’, with ትእዛዘ as its accusative object.

sentences.t: ወርእሳ ፡ ለእከይ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ዘአብዛኅከ ፡ አንስተ ፡ ተዐዲወከ ፡ ሕጎ ፡ ወፍትሖ ፡ ወሥርዐቶ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ዘጸሐፈ ፡ ሙሴ ፡ ወወሀበክሙ ፡ ለእስራኤል ፡ ከመ ፡ ኢታውስቡ ፡ እምባዕደ ፡ ፍጥረት ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ እምዘመድክሙ ፡ ወቤተ ፡ አቡክሙ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይኩኑ ፡ ንጹሓነ ፡ ወቅዱሳነ ፡ ዘርእክሙ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይኅድር ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ምስሌክሙ ፤
sentences.l: And-head-its to-evil on-account-of that-you-multiplied wives, having-transgressed-you his-law and-his-judgment and-his-ordinance of-Lord which wrote Moses and-gave-to-you to-Israel, that not you-take-wives from-other creation except from-your-kin and-house-of your-father, that they-be pure and-holy your-seed, that may-dwell Lord with-you;
sentences.i: The chief of the evil is that you multiplied wives, transgressing the law, judgment and ordinance of the Lord, which Moses wrote and gave to you, Israel, so that you would not take wives from another people except from your own kin and your father’s house, so that your offspring might be pure and holy, and the Lord might dwell with you;
sentences.n: ወርእሳ ለእከይ ‘the head of evil’: ርእስ + -ሃ ‘its’, with ለ- introducing the owner (‘its head, of evil’), i.e. the worst of it. በእንተ ዘ- ‘because (of the fact) that’ + አብዛኅከ, 2ms perfect causative ‘you made many’. ተዐዲወከ is a gerund (2ms, ‘you having transgressed’) with three accusative objects ሕጎ, ፍትሖ, ሥርዐቶ (each + -ኦ ‘his’), the possessor given by ለእግዚኣብሔር. ዘጸሐፈ ሙሴ ‘which Moses wrote’; ወወሀበክሙ ‘and gave to you (pl.)’, with ለእስራኤል in apposition. ከመ ኢታውስቡ: ከመ + 2mp subjunctive of አውሰበ ‘take a wife’; ባዕደ ፍጥረት ‘another creation, i.e. another people’; ዘእንበለ ‘except’. ይኩኑ is plural while ዘርእክሙ ‘your seed’ is singular in form, a loose agreement. Compare Deuteronomy 17:17 (a king must not multiply wives), Deuteronomy 7:3–4 (no intermarriage).

sentences.t: ወአንተሰ ፡ አስተሐቀርከ ፡ ሕገ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይመስለከ ፡ ዘትጠበብ ፡ እምእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወትረክብ ፡ ብዙኀ ፡ ደቂቀ ፡ ተባዕተ ።
sentences.l: And-you-indeed you-despised law-of Lord while it-seems-to-you that-you-are-wise more-than-Lord and-you-will-find many sons male.
sentences.i: But you despised the law of the Lord, imagining that you were wiser than the Lord and would obtain many male sons.
sentences.n: ወአንተሰ = ወ- + አንተ ‘you’ + -ሰ (contrast). አስተሐቀርከ is a 2ms perfect in the Št stem, ‘treat as small, despise’ (the root sense is my inference) (?). እንዘ ይመስለከ ‘while it seems to you’: ይመስለከ = 3ms imperfect of መሰለ ‘seem, resemble’ + -ከ ‘to you’, followed by ዘ- ‘that’ and ትጠበብ ‘you are wise’ (2ms imperfect); እም- gives the comparison ‘more than’. ትረክብ ‘you will find, obtain’; ብዙኀ ደቂቀ ተባዕተ ‘many sons, male’ with accusative endings (ደቂቅ is the plural of ወልድ).

sentences.t: ወእበዲ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ይጠብብ ፡ እምጥበቢሁ ፡ ለእጓለ ፡ እመሕያው ፡ ወኢወሀበከ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ፫ ፡ ደቂቅ ፡ ፩ ፡ ዘነሥአ ፡ ክብርከ ፡ ለባዕድ ፡ ወረሰየ ፡ ማኅደሮ ፡ ለእግዚኣብሔር ፡ ውስተ ፡ ብሔረ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፤
sentences.l: And-foolishness for-Lord is-wise more-than-his-wisdom of-offspring-of the-living, and-not-he-gave-you except 3 sons: 1 who took your-glory to-a-stranger and-made his-dwelling for-Lord in land-of Ethiopia;
sentences.i: And the foolishness of God is wiser than the wisdom of man, and he gave you only three sons: one who took your glory to a stranger and made the Lord’s dwelling in the land of Ethiopia;
sentences.n: ወእበዲ ለእግዚኣብሔር ‘the foolishness of God’: ለ- carries the owner after the noun (a construct paraphrase). ይጠብብ እም- ‘is wiser than’ (3ms imperfect with comparative እም-). This echoes 1 Corinthians 1:25 (‘the foolishness of God is wiser than men’). In እምጥበቢሁ ለእጓለ እመሕያው the suffix -ሁ ‘his’ anticipates the owner, who follows with ለ- (‘than his wisdom, of the son of man’). እጓለ እመሕያው is ‘offspring of the living’, a common phrase for ‘a human being, son of man’. ኢወሀበከ ‘he did not give you’ + ዘእንበለ ‘except’; the digits ፫ and ፩ are ‘three’ (ሠለስቱ) and ‘one’ (አሐዱ). ዘነሥአ ‘who took’ and ወረሰየ ‘and made’ are perfects with future (prophetic) sense: by the story’s logic this is Menelik (the text does not name him here). ለባዕድ ‘to a stranger, foreign (land)’. ማኅደሮ = ማኅደር ‘dwelling’ + -ኦ ‘his’ (accusative), ብሔረ ኢትዮጵያ ‘the land of Ethiopia’.

sentences.t: ወ፩ ፡ ፅዉሰ ፡ እግር ፡ ዘይከውን ፡ ዲበ ፡ መንበርከ ፡ ለነገደ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ወልደ ፡ ዘመደ ፡ ዘመድከ ፡ ተርባነ ፡ እምቤተ ፡ ይሁዳ ፤
sentences.l: And-1 lame(?)-of foot who-will-be upon your-throne for-tribe-of Israel, son-of kin-of your-kin, ተርባነ, from house-of Judah;
sentences.i: and one lame (?) in the foot, who will be upon your throne over the tribe of Israel, a son of the kin of your kin, ተርባነ (unclear), from the house of Judah;
sentences.n: ወ፩ = ወ- + ፩ ‘one’, continuing the list of three sons. ፅዉሰ ‘lame (?)’ is the construct of ፅዉስ, here before እግር ‘foot’ (‘lame-of foot’). ዘይከውን ‘who will be’ (3ms imperfect of ኮነ) + ዲበ መንበርከ ‘upon your throne’. ለነገደ እስራኤል: ነገድ is in the construct ‘tribe-of’, with the ለ- of ‘for/over’. ወልደ ዘመደ ዘመድከ is a stacked construct, ‘son-of kin-of your-kin’. I cannot identify ተርባነ (?); it may be an ethnic or titular noun or a corruption, so I left it unrendered. The text does not name this son, and I do not identify him.

sentences.t: ወ፩ ፡ ወልደ ፡ ሮማዊት ፡ አመት ፡ ዘበደኃሪ ፡ መዋዕል ፡ ይሤርዎ ፡ ለዮርብዓም ፡ ወለኵሉ ፡ ዘመድከ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ወትከውን ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ዛቲ ፡ ምድር ፡ እስመ ፡ ለሊሁ ፡ የአምን ፡ በዘ ፡ ይመጽእ ፡ መድኅን ፤
sentences.l: And-1 son-of Roman maidservant who in-last days he-will-uproot-him Jeroboam and-all your-kin Israel, and-will-be to-him this land, for he-himself he-believes in-him who-comes savior;
sentences.i: and one, the son of a Roman maidservant, who in the last days will uproot Jeroboam and all your kin of Israel; and this land will be his, for he himself believes in the one who is to come, the Saviour;
sentences.n: ሮማዊት is the feminine of ሮማዊ ‘Roman’, qualifying አመት ‘maidservant’; I do not know whom the text means (?). ዘበደኃሪ መዋዕል ‘who in the last days’. ይሤርዎ = ይሤርው (3ms imperfect of ሠረወ ‘uproot, destroy’) + -ኦ ‘him’, the object restated by ለዮርብዓም ‘Jeroboam’; the form could also be 3mp (‘they will uproot him’), and I take it as 3ms (?). ዮርብዓም is Jeroboam, first king of the breakaway northern kingdom (1 Kings 12), a type of rebellious Israel. ትከውን ሎቱ ‘will be to him’ (3fs, agreeing with ምድር); ዛቲ ‘this’ (feminine). የአምን በ- ‘he believes in’; መድኅን ‘Saviour’ (one who saves) is Christ.

sentences.t: ወነገደ ፡ ዮርብዓምሰ ፡ ወእለ ፡ ተርፉ ፡ እስራኤል ፡ ይሰቅልዎ ፡ ለዘ ፡ ይመጽእ ፡ መድኅን ፡ ወይጠፍእ ፡ ዝክርክሙ ፡ እምነ ፡ ምድር ፡ እስመ ፡ ይኄልዩ ፡ ምክረ ፡ እንተ ፡ ኢይክሉ ፡ አቅሞ ፡ ወውእቱኒ ፡ ይትመዓዖሙ ፡ ወያጠፍእ ፡ ዝክሮሙ ።
sentences.l: And-tribe-of Jeroboam-indeed and-those who remain Israel they-will-crucify-him, the-one who comes savior, and-will-perish your-memorial from earth, for they-plan a-plan which not they-can to-establish-it, and-he-also he-is-angry-with-them and-destroys their-memorial.
sentences.i: But the tribe of Jeroboam and those of Israel who are left will crucify the one who is to come, the Saviour, and your memorial will perish from the earth, because they devise a plan they cannot carry out; and he too will be angry with them and destroy their memorial.
sentences.n: ነገደ ዮርብዓምሰ: -ሰ marks the contrast with the previous clause. ተርፉ ‘remained’ is a 3mp perfect (ተረፈ). ይሰቅልዎ = ይሰቅሉ (3mp imperfect/subjunctive of ሰቀለ ‘hang, crucify’) + -ኦ ‘him’, the object restated by ለዘ ይመጽእ ‘the one who comes’. ይጠፍእ ‘will perish’ (intransitive) versus ያጠፍእ ‘will destroy’ (causative, አ- stem). ዝክርክሙ ‘your memorial’ becomes ዝክሮሙ ‘their memorial’ at the end: the writer shifts person. ይኄልዩ ምክረ ‘they devise a plan’ (cognate accusative); እንተ ‘which’ (feminine, so ምክር is taken as feminine here); አቅሞ = infinitive of አቀመ ‘establish’ (the final -ኦ may be the infinitive’s own ending rather than ‘it’). ይትመዓዖሙ = ይትመዓዕ ‘he is angry’ + -ሙ ‘them’ (?).

sentences.t: ወለከሰ ፡ ይኩንከ ፡ ትእምርተ ፡ ዮሴፍ ፡ ወልደ ፡ ያዕቆብ ፡ እስመ ፡ ሤጥዎ ፡ አኀዊሁ ፡ ብሔረ ፡ ግብጽ ፡ እምሶርያ ፡ ሀገረ ፡ ላባ ፡ ወበርደቱ ፡ ብሔረ ፡ ግብጽ ፡ ኮነ ፡ ረኃብ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሶርያ ፡ ወውስተ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ዓለም ፡ ወበርደቱ ፡ ጸውዖሙ ፡ ለአዝማዲሁ ፡ ወአድኀኖሙ ፡ እምረኃብ ፡ ወወሀቦሙ ፡ ማኅደረ ፡ በምድረ ፡ ግብጽ ፡ እንተ ፡ ስማ ፡ ጌሤን ፡ እስመ ፡ ለሊሁ ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ እምታሕተ ፡ ፈርዖን ፡ ንጉሠ ፡ ግብጽ ።
sentences.l: And-for-you-indeed let-be-to-you sign Joseph son-of Jacob, for they-sold-him his-brothers land-of Egypt from-Syria city-of Laban, and-at-his-descent land-of Egypt was famine in Syria and-in all world, and-at-his-descent he-called to-his-kin and-saved-them from-famine and-gave-them dwelling in-land-of Egypt which its-name Goshen, for he-himself king beneath Pharaoh king-of Egypt.
sentences.i: But for you, let Joseph the son of Jacob be a sign, for his brothers sold him to the land of Egypt from Syria, the city of Laban; and when he went down to the land of Egypt, there was a famine in Syria and throughout the world; and when he went down he called his kin and saved them from the famine and gave them a dwelling in the land of Egypt, whose name is Goshen, for he himself was king beneath Pharaoh, the king of Egypt.
sentences.n: ወለከሰ = ወ- + ለከ ‘to you’ + -ሰ (contrast). ይኩንከ = ይኩን, 3ms jussive of ኮነ (‘let it be’), + -ከ ‘to you’; ትእምርተ ‘a sign’ (accusative predicate). ሤጥዎ = ሤጠ ‘sold’, 3mp perfect (here -ው-ኦ contracted), + -ኦ ‘him’; አኀዊሁ ‘his brothers’. ብሔረ ግብጽ ‘to the land of Egypt’ is an accusative of direction. ወበርደቱ = ወ- + በ- ‘at’ + ርደት ‘descent’ + -ሁ ‘his’. Verbs of Joseph’s deeds are 3ms perfects with -ሙ ‘them’: ጸውዖሙ, አድኀኖሙ, ወሀቦሙ. እንተ ስማ ‘whose name (fem.)’, ሀገረ ላባ ‘city of Laban’. The text sets the sale in Syria, which differs from Genesis; the story is Genesis 37 and 41–47 (Goshen, Genesis 45:10).

sentences.t: ወከማሁ ፡ ዘይመጽእ ፡ መድኅን ፡ እምዘመድከ ፡ ይሰሪ ፡ ለከ ፡ በምጽአቱ ፡ ወያወፅአከ ፡ እምሲኦል ፤
sentences.l: And-likewise he-who comes savior from-your-kin he-will-forgive for-you at-his-coming and-bring-you-out from-Sheol;
sentences.i: And in the same way the one who is to come, the Saviour, from your kin, will forgive you (?) at his coming and bring you out of Sheol;
sentences.n: From here the chapter applies the type: ወከማሁ = ወ- ‘and’ + ከማሁ ‘likewise, in the same way’ (ከማ- + -ሁ), the answer to every በከመ ‘as’ clause below. ዘይመጽእ መድኅን ‘who comes, a saviour’; ይሰሪ is the 3ms imperfect of ሰርየ ‘forgive’ (?), with ለከ ‘for you’; ‘forgive for you’ is my reading of the construction (?). በምጽአቱ = በ- ‘at’ + ምጽአት ‘coming’ + -ሁ ‘his’. ያወፅአከ = causative (አወፅአ ‘bring out’) 3ms, with -ከ ‘you’. ሲኦል is Sheol, the place of the dead, which the text calls hell in a Christian sense.

sentences.t: ወእስከ ፡ ይመጽእ ፡ መድኅን ፡ ትሣቀይ ፡ በህየ ፡ ምስለ ፡ አበዊከ ፡ ወያወፅአከ ፤
sentences.l: And-until he-comes savior you-suffer there with-your-fathers and-he-will-bring-you-out;
sentences.i: and until the Saviour comes you will suffer there with your fathers, and he will bring you out;
sentences.n: ወእስከ ‘and until’ + ይመጽእ ‘he comes’ (subjunctive). ትሣቀይ is the 2ms imperfect of ሠቀየ ‘suffer, be in distress’, taking the sense ‘you will be in torment’ (?). በህየ ‘there’; ምስለ አበዊከ ‘with your fathers’ (አበው + -ከ). The picture is that Solomon and his fathers wait in Sheol until the Saviour releases them, the ‘harrowing of hell’ of Christian tradition.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ እምዘርእከ ፡ ይመጽእ ፡ መድኅን ፡ ዘያድኅነክሙ ፡ ለከ ፡ ወለእለ ፡ እምቅድሜከ ፡ ወለእለ ፡ እምድኅሬከ ፡ እምአዳም ፡ እስከ ፡ ምጽአቱ ፡ በዘመደ ፡ ዘመድክሙ ፡ ወያወፅአክሙ ፡ እምሲኦል ፤
sentences.l: For from-your-seed he-comes savior who he-will-save-you to-you and-to-those from-before-you and-to-those from-after-you from-Adam until his-coming by-kin-of your-kin and-he-will-bring-you-out from-Sheol;
sentences.i: for from your seed will come a Saviour who will save you, and those before you and those after you, from Adam until his coming, through the line of your kin, and he will bring you out of Sheol;
sentences.n: እምዘርእከ ‘from your seed’ (ዘርእ + -ከ). ዘያድኅነክሙ ‘who will save you (pl.)’: ዘ- + 3ms imperfect of አድኀነ + -ክሙ, followed by ለከ ‘to you (sg.)’ and ወለእለ ‘and to those who’, with እምቅድሜከ ‘from before you’ and እምድኅሬከ ‘from after you’. እምአዳም እስከ ምጽአቱ ‘from Adam until his coming’. በዘመደ ዘመድክሙ ‘by the kin of your kin’ is a stacked construct. The switch between ‘you’ singular (ከ) and plural (ክሙ) is the writer’s: Solomon first, then all those he represents.

sentences.t: በከመ ፡ አውፅኦሙ ፡ ዮሴፍ ፡ ለአዝማዲሁ ፡ እምረኃብ ፡ እስመ ፡ ቀዳሚት ፡ ሲኦል ፡ በምድረ ፡ ረኃብ ፡ ወከማሁ ፡ ያወፅአክሙ ፡ መድኅን ፡ እምሲኦል ፡ ለአዝማዲሁ ፤
sentences.l: As he-brought-them-out Joseph to-his-kin from-famine, for first Sheol in-land-of famine, and-likewise he-will-bring-you-out savior from-Sheol to-his-kin;
sentences.i: As Joseph brought his kin out of the famine (for the first Sheol was in a land of famine), so the Saviour will bring you out of Sheol, you who are his kin;
sentences.n: The type-and-antitype frame: በከመ ‘as, according as’ + a perfect (አውፅኦሙ ‘he brought them out’, causative + -ሙ), answered by ወከማሁ ‘and likewise’ + an imperfect (ያወፅአክሙ ‘he will bring you out’). Expect this pattern in each unit that follows. ለአዝማዲሁ ‘to his kin’ (አዝማድ ‘kin’ + -ሁ) restates the object. ቀዳሚት ሲኦል ‘the first Sheol’, i.e. the land of famine from which Joseph rescued his kin, taken as a figure of the underworld; በምድረ ረኃብ ‘in the land of famine’ (ምድር in construct).

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ቀነይዎሙ ፡ ድኅረ ፡ ግብጻዊያን ፡ ከማሁ ፡ ቀነዩክሙ ፡ አጋንንት ፡ በስሕተተ ፡ ጣዖት ፤
sentences.l: And-as they-enslaved-them afterwards Egyptians, likewise they-enslaved-you demons through-error-of idol;
sentences.i: And as the Egyptians afterwards enslaved them, so the demons enslaved you through the error of idolatry;
sentences.n: ቀነይዎሙ = ቀነየ ‘serve, subject to servitude’ (‘serve’ in the G stem; the transitive sense ‘enslave, subject’ is from context (?)), 3mp perfect (ቀነዩ) + -ሙ ‘them’; ቀነዩክሙ is the same verb + -ክሙ ‘you’. ድኅረ ‘afterwards’; ግብጻዊያን ‘Egyptians’ is the plural of ግብጻዊ; አጋንንት ‘demons’ (plural). ስሕተተ ጣዖት is a construct chain ‘error-of idol’; ጣዖት is a loanword for ‘idol’.

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ አውፅኦሙ ፡ ሙሴ ፡ ለአዝማዲሁ ፡ እምግብርናት ፡ ከማሁ ፡ ያወፅአክሙ ፡ መድኅን ፡ እምግብርናተ ፡ ሲኦል ፤
sentences.l: And-as he-brought-them-out Moses his-kin from-servitudes, likewise he-will-bring-you-out savior from-servitude-of Sheol;
sentences.i: And as Moses brought his kin out of slavery, so the Saviour will bring you out of the slavery of Sheol;
sentences.n: Same frame as before: በከመ + perfect አውፅኦሙ ‘he brought them out’, then ከማሁ + imperfect ያወፅአክሙ. ግብርናት ‘servitude’ is an abstract plural; its construct ግብርናተ gives ‘servitude-of Sheol’. The exodus from Egypt (Exodus 12–14) is the type.

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ገብረ ፡ ሙሴ ፡ ዐሠርተ ፡ ተኣምራተ ፡ ወመቅሠፍታተ ፡ በቅድመ ፡ ፈርዖን ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ከማሁ ፡ ዘይመጽእ ፡ መድኅን ፡ እምዘመድከ ፡ ይገብር ፡ ፲ ፡ ተኣምራተ ፡ ለሕይወት ፡ በቅድመ ፡ ሕዝብከ ፤
sentences.l: And-as he-did Moses ten wonders and-plagues before Pharaoh king, likewise he-who comes savior from-your-kin he-will-do 10 wonders for-life before your-people;
sentences.i: And as Moses worked ten wonders and plagues before Pharaoh the king, so the Saviour who will come from your kin will work ten wonders for life before your people;
sentences.n: ገብረ ‘did, made’ (3ms perfect) with ዐሠርተ ‘ten’ (feminine-looking accusative form), ተኣምራተ ‘wonders, miracles’ and መቅሠፍታተ ‘plagues, scourges’ (accusative plurals). በቅድመ ‘before’ takes ፈርዖን. ዘይመጽእ መድኅን as before; ይገብር ‘he will do’ (3ms imperfect) with ፲ ‘ten’. ለሕይወት ‘for life’ is set against the plagues that brought death. The ten plagues are Exodus 7–12.

sentences.t: ወገቢሮ ፡ ትእምርታተ ፡ ሙሴ ፡ በከመ ፡ ዘበጠ ፡ ባሕረ ፡ ወአኅለፎሙ ፡ እንተ ፡ የብስ ፡ ከማሁ ፡ ዘይመጽእ ፡ መድኅን ፡ ይነስት ፡ አረፋቲሃ ፡ ለሲኦል ፡ ወያወ ፡ ፅአክሙ ፤
sentences.l: And-having-done signs Moses, as he-struck sea and-made-them-pass by dry-land, likewise he-who comes savior he-will-demolish its-walls(?) for-Sheol and-bring-you-out;
sentences.i: And as Moses, after working signs, struck the sea and led them across on dry land, so the Saviour who is to come will break down the walls (?) of Sheol and bring you out;
sentences.n: ገቢሮ is a gerund (3ms, ‘having done’) with ትእምርታተ ‘signs’; the subject Moses follows. ዘበጠ ባሕረ ‘struck the sea’ (3ms perfect; Exodus 14:16, 21). አኅለፎሙ = causative of ኀለፈ ‘pass’ + -ሙ ‘them’; እንተ የብስ ‘by dry (land)’ (እንተ is the feminine relative, so it may be ‘[the sea] which is dry’; I take a prepositional use) (?). ይነስት ‘he will break down’ is the 3ms of a verb whose meaning I am inferring from the context (?); አረፋቲሃ ለሲኦል ‘its walls, of Sheol’ (አረፍት, plural አረፋት, ‘wall, enclosure’, uncertain) (?). The scribe split a word: ያወ ፡ ፅአክሙ is ያወፅአክሙ ‘he will bring you out’. Compare Psalm 107:16 (the gates of bronze broken).

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ አስጠሞ ፡ ሙሴ ፡ ለፈርዖን ፡ ምስለ ፡ ግብጻዊያን ፡ ውስተ ፡ ባሕረ ፡ ኤርትራ ፡ ከማሁ ፡ ያሰጥሞሙ ፡ ለሰይጣን ፡ ወለአጋንንቲሁ ፡ መድኅን ፡ ውስተ ፡ ሲኦል ፡ እስመ ፡ ባሕር ፡ ትተረጐም ፡ በሲኦል ፡ ወፈርዖን ፡ ይተረጐም ፡ በሰይጣን ፡ ወሰራዊቱ ፡ ግብጻዊያን ፡ ይተረጐሙ ፡ በአጋንንት ፤
sentences.l: And-as he-drowned Moses Pharaoh with Egyptians in sea-of Erythra, likewise he-will-drown them Satan and-his-demons savior in Sheol, for sea it-is-interpreted as-Sheol, and-Pharaoh it-is-interpreted as-Satan, and-his-army Egyptians they-are-interpreted as-demons;
sentences.i: And as Moses drowned Pharaoh with the Egyptians in the Red Sea, so the Saviour will drown Satan and his demons in Sheol; for the sea is to be understood as Sheol, Pharaoh as Satan, and his army, the Egyptians, as the demons;
sentences.n: አስጠሞ = causative of ሰጠመ ‘sink, drown’ (አስጠሞ being አሰጠመ with the vowel dropped) (?), 3ms perfect, + -ኦ ‘him’; ያሰጥሞሙ is the imperfect + -ሙ ‘them’; ለፈርዖን and ለሰይጣን restate the objects. ባሕረ ኤርትራ ‘sea of Erythra’ is the name used for the Red Sea (Exodus 14). The explanation clause uses the T-stem of ተረጐመ ‘interpret’: ትተረጐም (3fs), ይተረጐም (3ms), ይተረጐሙ (3mp), each ‘is interpreted’ with በ- ‘as, by means of’. ወሰራዊቱ ግብጻዊያን: ሰራዊት ‘army’ + -ሁ, with ‘the Egyptians’ in apposition.

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ሴሰዮሙ ፡ መና ፡ በገዳም ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ጻማ ፡ ከማሁ ፡ ይሴስየክሙ ፡ መድኅን ፡ መብልዐ ፡ ገነት ፡ ዘለዓለም ፡ እምድኅረ ፡ አውፅአክሙ ፡ እምሲኦል ፤
sentences.l: And-as he-fed-them manna in-wilderness without toil, likewise he-will-feed-you savior food-of garden eternal after he-brought-you-out from-Sheol;
sentences.i: And as he fed them manna in the wilderness without toil, so the Saviour will feed you the food of the eternal garden, after he has brought you out of Sheol;
sentences.n: ሴሰዮሙ = ሴሰየ ‘feed’ (3ms perfect) + -ሙ ‘them’; ይሴስየክሙ is the imperfect + -ክሙ ‘you’. መና is manna (Exodus 16). ዘእንበለ ጻማ ‘without toil’. መብልዐ ገነት ‘food-of garden’ is a construct chain, and ዘለዓለም ‘of eternity, eternal’ qualifies it; ገነት ‘garden’ is paradise. እምድኅረ አውፅአክሙ ‘after he brought you out’ (እምድኅረ + perfect).

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ አንበሮሙ ፡ በገዳም ፡ ፵ ፡ ዓመተ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ኢበልየ ፡ አልባሲሆሙ ፡ ወኢነቅዐ ፡ ሰኰናሆሙ ፡ ከማሁ ፡ መድኅን ፡ ያነብረክሙ ፡ ዘእንበለ ፡ ጻማ ፡ እምድኅረ ፡ ትንሣኤ ፤
sentences.l: And-as he-made-them-dwell in-wilderness 40 years while not-wore-out their-garments and-not-swelled their-hooves, likewise savior he-will-make-you-dwell without toil after resurrection;
sentences.i: And as he made them dwell in the wilderness forty years, while their clothes did not wear out and their feet did not swell (?), so the Saviour will make you dwell without toil after the resurrection;
sentences.n: አንበሮሙ = causative of ነበረ ‘sit, dwell’ + -ሙ ‘them’; ያነብረክሙ is the imperfect + -ክሙ. ፵ ዓመተ ‘forty years’ (accusative of duration). እንዘ + ኢበልየ ‘while … not wore out’ (3ms perfect, singular verb with the plural subject አልባሲሆሙ ‘their garments’). ኢነቅዐ: I read ‘did not swell’ because of Deuteronomy 8:4 (‘your clothing did not wear out nor did your feet swell’); the verb ነቅዐ is more usually ‘gush, burst forth’, so this is inferred (?). ሰኰና is ‘hoof, sole, foot’. ትንሣኤ ‘resurrection’.

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ አብኦሙ ፡ ኢየሱስ ፡ ምድረ ፡ ርስት ፡ ከማሁ ፡ ያበውአክሙ ፡ መድኅን ፡ ውስተ ፡ ገነተ ፡ ትፍሥሕት ፤
sentences.l: And-as he-brought-them-in Joshua land-of inheritance, likewise he-will-bring-you-in savior into garden-of joy;
sentences.i: And as Joshua brought them into the land of inheritance, so the Saviour will bring you into the garden of joy;
sentences.n: አብኦሙ = causative of ቦአ ‘enter’ (‘bring in’), 3ms perfect + -ሙ; ያበውአክሙ is the imperfect + -ክሙ. ኢየሱስ here is Joshua (the Greek and Geʿez form of the name, the same as Jesus), who led Israel into Canaan, so the type fits; ምድረ ርስት ‘land-of inheritance’. ገነተ ትፍሥሕት ‘garden-of joy’ is another construct chain.

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ ቀተሎሙ ፡ ኢየሱስ ፡ ለ፯ ፡ ነገሥተ ፡ ከነአን ፡ ከማሁ ፡ ይቀትሎሙ ፡ መድኅን ፡ ለሰብዐቱ ፡ አርእስተ ፡ አብሊስ ፤
sentences.l: And-as he-killed-them Joshua the-seven kings-of Canaan, likewise he-will-kill-them savior the-seven heads-of the-Devil;
sentences.i: And as Joshua killed the seven kings of Canaan, so the Saviour will kill the seven heads of the Devil;
sentences.n: ቀተሎሙ = ቀተለ ‘kill’ (3ms perfect) + -ሙ ‘them’; ይቀትሎሙ is the imperfect. ለ፯ is ለ- + ፯ ‘seven’, spoken ሰብዐቱ (written out in the second half: ለሰብዐቱ አርእስተ አብሊስ ‘the seven heads of Iblis’). The seven nations of Canaan are listed in Deuteronomy 7:1; the seven heads may recall the seven-headed dragon of Revelation 12:3 (?). አብሊስ is the Devil (the form of the name known from Arabic, Iblis).

sentences.t: ወከመ ፡ ሠረዎሙ ፡ ኢያሱ ፡ ለሕዝበ ፡ ከነኦን ፡ ከማሁ ፡ ይሤርዎሙ ፡ መድኅን ፡ ለኃጥኣን ፡ ወየኀትሞሙ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ማኅተመ ፡ ሲኦል ፤
sentences.l: And-as he-uprooted-them Joshua people-of Canaan, likewise he-will-uproot-them savior sinners and-seal-them in seal-of Sheol;
sentences.i: And as Joshua uprooted the people of Canaan, so the Saviour will uproot the sinners and seal them in the seal of Sheol;
sentences.n: ወከመ ‘and as’ (without በ-). ሠረዎሙ = ሠረወ ‘uproot, destroy’ (3ms perfect) + -ሙ; ይሤርዎሙ is the 3ms imperfect ይሤርው + -ሙ. Here ኢያሱ is again Joshua and ኢየሱስ above is the same man; the text uses both spellings. ሕዝበ ከነኦን ‘people-of Canaan’ (ከነኦን, a variant spelling of ከነአን above). ወየኀትሞሙ = 3ms imperfect of ኀተመ ‘seal’ + -ሙ; ማኅተመ ሲኦል ‘seal-of Sheol’, i.e. the locking-up of the damned (compare Revelation 20:3).

sentences.t: ወበከመ ፡ አንተ ፡ ሐነጽከ ፡ ቤተ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ከማሁ ፡ ይትሐነጽ ፡ አብያተ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ውስተ ፡ አርእስተ ፡ አድባር ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: And-as you built house-of Lord, likewise will-be-built houses-of Lord on heads-of mountains.
sentences.i: And as you built the house of the Lord, so the houses of the Lord will be built on the tops of the mountains.
sentences.n: ሐነጽከ ‘you built’ (2ms perfect of ሐነጸ), the last of the as-clauses, with Solomon himself as the figure: his temple is the type of the churches. ይትሐነጽ is the 3ms imperfect passive (T-stem) ‘will be built’, with a plural subject አብያተ ‘houses-of’ (construct) እግዚኣብሔር. አርእስተ አድባር ‘heads-of mountains’ (ደብር ‘mountain’, plural አድባር). Compare Isaiah 2:2 and Micah 4:1 (the house of the Lord on the top of the mountains). The string ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ is the closing ornament of the chapter.
